outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the main development is a preprint (arXiv 2606.01609, posted 1 June 2026, revised 26 September 2026) by Adams, Ionov, Mason-Brown and Vogan claiming that every Arthur packet of a real reductive group consists of unitary representations (Arthur's unitarity conjecture for real groups), and that Jiang's wavefront conjecture follows for real groups; it has no human expert verification on record, only two automated AI-referee reviews. The global multiplicity formula for reductive groups in general and the non-archimedean unitarity question are not settled by anything in the window; the other in-window work is partial, concerns an analogue (metaplectic, unitary, function-field), or concerns a neighbouring conjecture.
problem_asks: The bullet names only "Arthur's conjectures" and links the Wikipedia article of that name; it lists no sub-part. Read through that article's lead (a stub: conjectures of James Arthur, 1989, on automorphic representations of reductive groups over adele rings and on unitary representations of reductive groups over local fields, motivated by the Arthur-Selberg trace formula; they imply the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for cusp forms on GL_n). Parts the statement demands, as I read it: (a) GLOBAL: for a connected reductive group over a number field, the discrete automorphic spectrum decomposes into global Arthur packets indexed by global Arthur parameters, with Arthur's multiplicity formula for the multiplicities. (b) LOCAL: for a connected reductive group over a local field, local Arthur packets attached to local Arthur parameters, with their character identities and endoscopic properties. (c) UNITARITY: the representations in Arthur packets are unitary, for real groups and for non-archimedean local fields (the lead says 'unitary representations ... over local fields'). (d) UNIPOTENT CASE: the 1989 conjectures on unipotent automorphic representations and their parameters (Astérisque 171-172). (e) CONSEQUENCES the lead names: the generalized Ramanujan bound for cusp forms on GL_n. The statement itself does not say which of these is meant; this reading is taken from the linked article and is the thing a later pass should check.

events.what_happened: James Arthur, 'The Endoscopic Classification of Representations: Orthogonal and Symplectic Groups', AMS Colloquium Publications vol. 61 (2013). Gives the endoscopic classification of the discrete automorphic spectrum and of local packets for quasi-split special orthogonal and symplectic groups (trivial similitude factor, per the secondary summary I found). Book, not opened; its content is taken from a later paper's description (arXiv 2410.13504 abstract, opened) and a search summary of the AMS catalogue record.
events.revisions: An earlier draft exists on Arthur's website (file name 'arthur-endoscopic-2012.pdf', seen in search results, not opened); its posting date was not established.
events.delivers: Endoscopic classification for quasi-split SO and Sp of arbitrary rank (trivial similitude factor), over number fields and over local fields of characteristic zero. The classification is an inductive argument that later work describes as conditional on inputs (co-tempered packets and the weighted fundamental lemma; see atobe-gan-ichino-kaletha-minguez-shin-2024).
events.remains: Quasi-split groups outside SO/Sp with trivial similitude factor, non-quasi-split groups, GSpin and similitude groups, and the general multiplicity formula for reductive groups in general.
events.time_since_posted: Not applicable; later work builds on it (see later_work_cites_it).
events.doubts: The book's inductive proof depends on inputs that later work has partly removed (co-tempered A-packets, now proved in arXiv 2410.13504 as opened) and on the twisted weighted fundamental lemma, which that paper still assumes.
events.direction: Confirms Arthur's conjectural global and local classification for quasi-split SO and Sp (the classical part of the problem).

events.what_happened: Stephen D. Miller, 'Residual automorphic forms and spherical unitary representations of exceptional groups', arXiv:1205.0426, submitted 2 May 2012; published Annals of Mathematics 177(3), 2013 (publication per search snippet, not opened). Abstract (opened): 'Arthur has conjectured that the unitarity of a number of representations can be shown'; extends earlier spherical results to E6, E7, E8, F4; 'we prove Arthur's conjecture that the spherical constituent of an unramified principal series' is unitary.
events.delivers: Unitarity of the spherical (unramified) constituent of an unramified principal series of a Chevalley group, for the exceptional groups E6, E7, E8 and F4 (classical groups by Moeglin, G2 by Kim, per the abstract's context), over local fields of characteristic zero, under a condition on the Langlands parameter (condition as given in the Annals abstract seen in search, not opened).
events.remains: Non-spherical constituents of unramified principal series, non-unramified packets, and non-split forms.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper, vol. 177 issue 3 (2013) (seen in search results, not opened)

events.doubts: The exceptional-group case rests on computer calculations; the arXiv abstract says the computational data and programs are on the author's website, and does not say what the computer verified. Later work (hegde-2026) describes the earlier cases as 'proved in 2013 using computers by Miller'. This is computer-assisted, not AI.
events.direction: Confirms Arthur's conjecture for the spherical unramified case, for the listed exceptional groups.

events.what_happened: Joseph Hundley and Stephen D. Miller, 'On Arthur's unitarity conjecture for split real groups', arXiv:1908.04363, v1 12 Aug 2019; v2 4 Aug 2021; v3 15 Jul 2026 (updated posting adding comments on normalized intertwining operators, described as a post-publication version). Current abstract (v3, opened): they prove 'the unitarity of the Langlands element (i.e., the one specified by Arthur) of all unipotent Arthur packets for split real groups'. The v1 abstract (opened) says the same for split real groups. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.revisions: v2 4 Aug 2021; v3 15 Jul 2026 (in window; comments added, the abstract still states the split-real-groups result).
events.delivers: Unitarity of one distinguished member (the Langlands element) of each unipotent Arthur packet for split real groups. Method: Eisenstein series, Langlands' constant term formula, square-integrability criterion and intertwining operators, with Dirichlet L-function input, reducing to a combinatorial statement about intertwining operators.
events.remains: The other members of each packet (the abstract makes no claim about them); non-unipotent Arthur packets; non-split real groups; non-archimedean fields.
events.doubts: The arXiv page gives no journal reference, and the v3 comment calls it a 'post-publication version' without naming a venue. An earlier search summary claimed the v1 scope was 'split over Q'; the fetched v1 abstract says 'split real groups', and I used the fetched text. Only the Langlands element is claimed, which a later paper (hegde-2026) relies on.
events.direction: Confirms a restricted case (the Langlands element of unipotent packets, split real groups) of Arthur's unitarity conjecture.

events.what_happened: Adams, van Leeuwen, Miller and Vogan (AMLV, also written AMvLV) show unitarity of special unipotent representations for real forms of exceptional groups, using the atlas software. Dated only indirectly: the Mason-Brown and Matvieievskyi abstract (arXiv:2109.09124 v1, 19 Sep 2021, opened) credits 'the work of Adams-Miller-van Leeuwen-Vogan' for this, so the result existed by that date. A JMM 2023 talk 'Enumeration and unitarity of Arthur's representations for exceptional real groups' (Vogan with Adams, van Leeuwen, Miller) is listed in search results; its slides were unreadable through the fetcher. The AMLV paper itself was not found and its posting date is unknown.
events.revisions: Unknown. The date given is an upper bound from the 2021 citation, not the first public written argument.
events.delivers: Unitarity of special unipotent representations (and, per arXiv:2109.09124, of the unipotent representations attached to rigid orbits) for all real forms of exceptional groups including E8(R), by atlas computation. Per arXiv:2606.01609 (AIMV), this is one of the sources for the unipotent case that its Jordan decomposition reduces to.
events.remains: Non-unipotent Arthur packets for these groups, and classical groups (handled by other authors).
events.doubts: The written proof was not located, so the claim is known only through citations and talk material. The atlas computations are computer work, not AI.
events.direction: Confirms unitarity for the unipotent case on exceptional groups (a case of Arthur's unitarity conjecture, as the cited papers use it).

events.what_happened: Lucas Mason-Brown and Dmytro Matvieievskyi, 'Unipotent Ideals for Spin and Exceptional Groups', arXiv:2109.09124, v1 19 Sep 2021, v2 22 Sep 2021 (opened). Defines unipotent representations of a real reductive group attached to rigid nilpotent orbits; shows that for real forms of simple exceptional groups these are all unitary, using atlas software and AMLV. Also computes infinitesimal characters of unipotent ideals for spin and exceptional groups and proves Vogan's conjecture that unipotent ideals are maximal.
events.revisions: v2 22 Sep 2021 (in the abstract as opened, no later version found).
events.delivers: Unitarity of unipotent representations attached to rigid nilpotent orbits, for real forms of simple exceptional groups. These are building blocks of the unitary dual, not Arthur packets as such.
events.remains: Unitarity for real classical groups in this form, non-rigid orbits, and all non-unipotent packets.
events.doubts: The unitarity claim depends on atlas computations and on the AMLV work it cites.
events.direction: Confirms unitarity for a class of unipotent representations (rigid orbits, exceptional real groups), adjacent to Arthur's unitarity conjecture.

events.what_happened: Rui Chen and Jialiang Zou, 'Arthur's multiplicity formula for even orthogonal and unitary groups', arXiv:2103.07956, v1 14 Mar 2021, v3 21 Oct 2024 (opened). Abstract: proves Arthur's multiplicity formula for the generic part of the automorphic discrete spectrum of an even orthogonal or unitary group over a number field, using theta lifts; gives a multiplicity formula for a class of non-generic A-parameters; describes the full discrete spectrum when the group has Witt index at most one. Journal: accepted by JEMS (arXiv comment); the EMS record (seen in search, not opened) gives JEMS 27(12) 2025, pp. 4769-4843.
events.revisions: v2 2 Feb 2022; v3 21 Oct 2024 (in window); journal publication 2025 per the EMS record seen in search.
events.delivers: Arthur's multiplicity formula for the generic part of the discrete spectrum of even orthogonal and unitary groups over number fields; for a class of non-generic parameters; full discrete spectrum when Witt index is at most one.
events.remains: The non-generic part outside the class treated; groups of Witt index at least two; other groups.

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (refereed)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper (arXiv comment); published JEMS 27(12) 2025 per the EMS record (seen in search, not opened)

events.doubts: The formula is proved only for the generic part and for Witt index at most one in the full statement, as the abstract states.
events.direction: Confirms Arthur's multiplicity formula for the listed classes (even orthogonal and unitary, generic part).

events.what_happened: Olivier Taibi, 'Arthur's multiplicity formula for certain inner forms of special orthogonal and symplectic groups', arXiv:1510.08395, first submitted 28 Oct 2015 (opened). Published JEMS 21(3) 2019, pp. 839-871 (per search snippet of the EMS page, not opened).
events.revisions: Single arXiv version (v1). Journal publication 2019 per search snippet.
events.delivers: Proves Arthur's multiplicity formula for automorphic representations of an SO_n or an inner form of Sp_2n over a number field, which is discrete series at a non-empty set S of real places and quasi-split elsewhere, under algebraic regular infinitesimal character at the places in S.
events.remains: Other inner forms; non-regular infinitesimal characters; the general case.
events.doubts: Restricted by the regular-character hypothesis at real places.
events.direction: Confirms Arthur's multiplicity formula for the listed inner forms, under the stated hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Hiroshi Ishimoto, 'The endoscopic classification of representations of non-quasi-split odd special orthogonal groups', arXiv:2301.12143, v1 28 Jan 2023, v2 16 Jun 2024 (opened). Follows Kaletha-Minguez-Shin-White. IMRN 2024 (Osaka list seen in search, not opened).
events.delivers: Endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split odd special orthogonal groups, restricted to generic parameters.
events.remains: Non-generic parameters for these groups; other non-quasi-split groups.
events.doubts: Restricted to generic parameters, as the abstract says.
events.direction: Confirms the endoscopic classification (a part of Arthur's conjectural framework) for the listed groups and parameters.

events.what_happened: Baiying Liu and Chi-Heng Lo, 'On the weak local Arthur packets conjecture for split classical groups', arXiv:2308.09648, first submitted 18 Aug 2023 (opened). IMRN 2024 no. 14, pp. 10708-10731 (per search snippet, not opened).
events.revisions: Single arXiv version. IMRN publication 2024 (search snippet).
events.delivers: Proves the weak local Arthur packets conjecture of Ciubotaru, Mason-Brown and Okada for split Sp_2n and split SO_2n+1 over p-adic fields, when the residue characteristic is large; implies unitarity of those unipotent representations (per the abstract).
events.remains: Small residue characteristic; non-split and non-classical groups.
events.doubts: Restricted to large residue characteristic.
events.direction: Confirms a p-adic, classical-group case of the local Arthur packet picture, under a residue-characteristic hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Wen-Wei Li, 'Stabilization of the trace formula for metaplectic groups', arXiv:2109.06581, v1 14 Sep 2021, v2 22 Dec 2023, v3 26 Mar 2024 (opened). Published as Astérisque 464 (2026), per a CiNii record seen in search (not opened).
events.revisions: v2 22 Dec 2023; v3 26 Mar 2024 (in window; 'further improvements and corrections').
events.delivers: Stabilization of the full Arthur-Selberg trace formula for the metaplectic cover of Sp_2n over a number field: a linear combination of stable trace formulas of products of split odd orthogonal groups. This is the trace-formula input for Arthur-type classification in the metaplectic case.
events.remains: The classification itself; it is a step, not a multiplicity formula. Metaplectic groups are not reductive.
events.doubts: Analogue setting (metaplectic), not the reductive-group statement.
events.direction: Analogue: a step of the trace-formula programme for metaplectic groups, not a claim about Arthur's conjectures for reductive groups.

events.what_happened: Hiraku Atobe, 'Construction of local A-packets', arXiv:2012.07232, v1 14 Dec 2020, v2 8 Apr 2021, v3 25 Apr 2022 ('Final version', opened). Restates Moeglin's explicit construction of local A-packets for split odd SO and Sp, computes them explicitly with Minguez's earlier work, gives a non-vanishing criterion, a derivative algorithm and an Aubert-dual formula.
events.delivers: Explicit computable local A-packets for split odd SO and Sp (the classical case of local Arthur packets).
events.remains: Non-split and other groups; the general local packet theory.
events.direction: Supports Arthur's local packet framework for split classical groups; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Nicolas Arancibia Robert and Paul Mezo, 'Equivalent definitions of Arthur packets for real unitary groups', arXiv:2204.10715, v1 22 Apr 2022, v2 15 Sep 2022 (opened). Proves that the harmonic-analysis definition (Mok; Moeglin-Renard) and the sheaf-theoretic ABV definition of Arthur packets agree for real unitary groups.
events.delivers: Equivalence of the two definitions of Arthur packets for real unitary groups.
events.remains: Other real groups; the unitarity of the packets so defined.
events.direction: Consistency result about the definition of Arthur packets for real unitary groups; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Alexander Hazeltine, Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo, 'On the intersection of local Arthur packets for classical groups and applications', arXiv:2201.10539, v1 25 Jan 2022, v2 5 Apr 2024, v3 15 Apr 2024 (opened). For Sp and split odd SO: operators, algorithms (with Sage code) deciding whether a representation is of Arthur type, and a formula for the set of parameters whose packets contain it.
events.revisions: v2 5 Apr 2024 and v3 15 Apr 2024 (in window).
events.delivers: Algorithmic description of intersections of local Arthur packets for split Sp and odd SO, and membership of representations in Arthur packets.
events.remains: Other groups; the enhanced Shahidi statement is not in the fetched abstract (a search summary claimed Section 9 proves it; I did not verify that).
events.doubts: Whether this version already proves the enhanced Shahidi conjecture is unclear from the abstract; see hazeltine-liu-lo-2024-enhanced-shahidi.
events.direction: Supports the local Arthur packet framework for classical groups.

events.what_happened: Alexander Hazeltine, Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo, 'On the enhanced Shahidi conjecture and global applications', arXiv:2404.05773, v1 8 Apr 2024, v2 29 Apr 2024, v3 18 Jun 2024 (opened; abstract page only). Abstract: for symplectic and split odd special orthogonal groups, 'the first complete proof of the enhanced Shahidi conjecture' (local Arthur packets are tempered iff they have generic members); classifies unramified representations of Arthur type, each lying in exactly one local Arthur packet, which is anti-generic; global applications. A search snippet gave an earlier title, 'Certain conjectures of Clozel and Shahidi on Arthur packets' (v2), not opened. No journal reference.
events.revisions: v2 29 Apr 2024; v3 18 Jun 2024. Earlier title per search snippet.
events.delivers: Complete proof of the enhanced Shahidi conjecture for Sp and split odd SO (local Arthur packets tempered iff containing generic members), and classification of unramified Arthur-type representations for these groups.
events.remains: Other groups; the enhanced Shahidi conjecture is a conjecture of Shahidi and Clozel about local Arthur packets, not an Arthur conjecture as such.
events.time_since_posted: About 2.5 years; no human verification found.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was read; the proof was not read. A later paper (hazeltine-liu-lo-2026-even-orthogonal) cites a result of this paper as 'HLL24, Theorem 1.2' in a search snippet, which I did not verify.
events.direction: Confirms a neighbouring conjecture (enhanced Shahidi) for the classical groups; not an Arthur conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Wen-Wei Li, 'Arthur packets for metaplectic groups', arXiv:2410.13606, v1 17 Oct 2024, v2 13 Nov 2024 ('Minor improvements', opened, abstract only). Local: for metaplectic groups over local fields of characteristic zero, an Arthur packet for each Arthur parameter as a multiset of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterised by endoscopic character relations. Global: a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete L2 spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and epsilon-factors, via the metaplectic trace formula; 'confirms a conjecture of Gan'.
events.delivers: Local Arthur packets and a global multiplicity formula, for metaplectic groups (the analogue of Arthur's framework for a non-reductive group).
events.remains: Reductive groups; the reductive-group multiplicity formula.
events.time_since_posted: About 12 months; no human verification found.
events.doubts: Analogue setting. The formula is a multiplicity formula in the metaplectic case, with an extra epsilon-factor; it is not the reductive-group formula.
events.direction: Analogue: Arthur-type packets and multiplicity formula for metaplectic groups; no counterexample to anything in the bullet.

events.what_happened: Hiraku Atobe, Wee Teck Gan, Atsushi Ichino, Tasho Kaletha, Alberto Minguez, Sug Woo Shin, 'Local Intertwining Relations and Co-tempered A-packets of Classical Groups', arXiv:2410.13504, v1 17 Oct 2024, v2 25 Jul 2025, v3 24 Jul 2026 (opened, abstract). Proves instances of the local intertwining relation for quasi-split classical groups and twisted GL_n; constructs co-tempered local A-packets by Aubert duality; 'Together with further technical results ... this makes the endoscopic classification conditional only on the validity of the twisted weighted fundamental lemma' (the Arthur-Mok classification for quasi-split classical groups).
events.delivers: Removes the co-tempered and intertwining inputs from the inductive proof of the endoscopic classification for quasi-split classical groups, leaving the twisted weighted fundamental lemma as the only assumption.
events.remains: The twisted weighted fundamental lemma (an assumption); the classification's statement for these groups is not new.
events.time_since_posted: About 12 months; no human verification found.
events.doubts: Conditional on the twisted weighted fundamental lemma; changes the status of the proof's hypotheses, not the statement of the classification.
events.direction: Changes a hypothesis of an existing classification (Arthur's endoscopic classification for quasi-split classical groups); no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Yeansu Kim, Muthu Krishnamurthy, Freydoon Shahidi, 'L-packets and the generic Arthur packet conjectures for even unitary similitude groups', arXiv:2506.00892, submitted 1 Jun 2025 (opened, abstract). Establishes the generic local Langlands correspondence for even unitary similitude groups (equality of Langlands-Shahidi and Artin L-functions) and proves weak and strong versions of the generic Arthur packet conjectures for even unitary similitude groups and even unitary groups; also describes non-generic L-packets, Shahidi's conjecture and finiteness of L-packets. Published Pacific J. Math. 344 (2026), pp. 367-393 (journal page seen in search, not opened).
events.revisions: Single arXiv version. PJM publication 2026 (search snippet).
events.delivers: Generic Arthur packet conjectures (weak and strong) for even unitary similitude and even unitary groups; generic local Langlands for even unitary similitude groups; L-packet properties for these groups.
events.remains: Odd unitary and other groups; the non-generic members of packets beyond the listed properties.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published vol. 344 no. 2 (2026); date seen in search (journal page not opened)

events.doubts: Generic part and even unitary groups only.
events.direction: Confirms the generic part of Arthur's packet conjectures for even unitary similitude and even unitary groups.

events.what_happened: Baiying Liu and Freydoon Shahidi, 'The Jiang conjecture on the wavefront sets of local Arthur packets', arXiv:2503.05343, submitted 7 Mar 2025 (opened, abstract). A progress report: partially proves Jiang's conjecture on the upper bound of nilpotent orbits in wavefront sets of representations in local Arthur packets of classical groups; under certain assumptions proves the enhanced Shahidi conjecture.
events.delivers: Partial results on Jiang's upper bound for wavefront sets of classical groups; enhanced Shahidi under unspecified assumptions.
events.remains: The full Jiang conjecture; the enhanced Shahidi statement in full generality.
events.doubts: Progress report; assumptions not stated in the abstract.
events.direction: Partial: Jiang's conjecture (not an Arthur conjecture) on wavefront sets in Arthur packets; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Baiying Liu and Freydoon Shahidi, 'On Jiang's wavefront sets conjecture for representations in local Arthur packets', arXiv:2603.13465, v1 13 Mar 2026, v2 6 May 2026 ('Strengthened the main result', opened, abstract). Reduces the upper-bound question for quasi-split classical groups to a property of bi-torsor representations of GL_n, implied by Atobe-Ciubotaru when the residue characteristic is large. The v2 comment says the underlying note 'was available around 2022' and links the 2025 report (arXiv:2503.05343).
events.delivers: Reduction of Jiang's upper bound (quasi-split classical groups) to a GL_n property, which holds when the residue characteristic is large.
events.remains: The full conjecture; small residue characteristic.
events.doubts: The v2 comment says the note 'was available around 2022'. If that earlier version was publicly written, the first written argument predates the window; I did not locate that earlier version.
events.direction: Partial reduction of Jiang's conjecture (not an Arthur conjecture); no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Alexander Hazeltine, Dihua Jiang, Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo, Qing Zhang, 'On Arthur representations and the unitary dual', arXiv:2410.11806, v1 15 Oct 2024, v2 16 May 2025, v3 1 Aug 2025, v4 9 Feb 2026 (opened, abstract). Proposes a conjecture describing the unitary dual of connected reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields in characteristic zero in terms of Arthur representations; gives an algorithm for classical groups; supports the conjecture (generic and unramified unitary duals, low corank) and verifies it for the unitary dual of G2.
events.delivers: A candidate set for the unitary dual of p-adic reductive groups built from Arthur representations, verified for G2 and supported elsewhere.
events.remains: The full conjecture for general G; the p-adic unitary dual outside the cases checked.
events.doubts: A conjecture, verified only for G2 and in the classical algorithm; the unitary dual question is related to but not the same as Arthur's unitarity conjecture.
events.direction: Proposes a conjecture about the unitary dual; verifies it for G2 (a finite instance of a conjecture about all groups, relevant only as context).

events.what_happened: Maxim Gurevich and Emile Okada, 'Ramification of weak Arthur packets for p-adic groups', arXiv:2404.03485, v1 4 Apr 2024, v2 25 Aug 2026 (opened, abstract). For split odd orthogonal and split symplectic p-adic groups: explicit decomposition of a weak Arthur packet into Arthur packets arising from endoscopic transfer, characterised by ramification of the constituents; introduces weak sphericity, linked to Lusztig's canonical quotients.
events.delivers: Explicit decomposition of weak Arthur packets for split odd SO and Sp over p-adic fields.
events.remains: Other groups; the general weak-packet conjecture.
events.direction: Neighbouring p-adic result on Arthur-type packets for classical groups; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Leticia Barchini and Andras C. Lorincz, 'Some unipotent Arthur packets for p-adic split F4', arXiv:2512.07014, submitted 7 Dec 2025 (opened, abstract). For split p-adic F4 and the minimal distinguished orbit F4(a3): computes characteristic cycles of the perverse sheaves IC(S, L), determines all micro-packets, shows the basic Arthur packet is a micro-packet, and that weak Arthur packets are unions of micro-packets (verifying a conjecture of Ciubotaru, Mason-Brown, Okada in this case).
events.delivers: Unipotent Arthur packets and weak Arthur packets for split p-adic F4 at the F4(a3) infinitesimal character only.
events.remains: Other orbits and other p-adic groups.
events.time_since_posted: About 10 months; no human verification found.
events.doubts: One group and one orbit. A third-party AI summary (themoonlight.io, seen in search, not opened) claims more; I did not verify that.
events.direction: Partial: one p-adic group, one orbit, of the local unipotent Arthur-packet picture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Jiahe Chen, 'Construction of Local Arthur Packets for Metaplectic Groups and the Adams Conjecture', arXiv:2603.11602, v1 12 Mar 2026, v2 26 Apr 2026 (opened, abstract). Explicit construction of local Arthur packets for metaplectic groups over non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero, generalising Atobe; proves they are multiplicity free; generalises Moeglin's work on the Adams conjecture to metaplectic groups.
events.delivers: Local Arthur packets for metaplectic groups: construction and multiplicity-freeness; generalisation of the Adams conjecture result to metaplectic groups.
events.remains: Reductive groups; the scope of the Adams-conjecture generalisation was not confirmed from the abstract.
events.doubts: Analogue setting (metaplectic).
events.direction: Analogue for metaplectic groups; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Alexander Hazeltine, Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo, 'The intersection of local Arthur packets for even orthogonal groups and applications', arXiv:2609.27261, submitted 23 Sep 2026 (opened, abstract). Algorithms to compute local Arthur packets and their intersections for even orthogonal groups over p-adic fields, and to decide membership; as applications: distinguished parameters, the closure ordering conjecture, the enhanced Shahidi conjecture, the weak local Arthur packet conjecture and the good parity unitary dual conjecture, for these groups.
events.delivers: Explicit local Arthur packets for even orthogonal groups over p-adic fields, and the listed conjectures for those groups (per the abstract).
events.remains: Other groups; non-p-adic fields.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 weeks; no human verification found.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was read; the claimed applications were not checked.
events.direction: Advances the local Arthur packet picture for even orthogonal groups; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Kristaps John Balodis, 'A short note on Arthur parameters with singular orbit closures', arXiv:2609.06793, v1 6 Sep 2026, sole author (opened: abstract and HTML). Proves each GL_n Arthur parameter over a p-adic field splits as a direct sum of Arthur parameters, and that its orbit closure in the Vogan variety is smooth exactly when each summand's closure is smooth, which holds exactly when the summand's orbit is open or closed. Not a conjecture of Arthur's. AI disclosure (author's statement in the HTML, quoted): 'All the theorems, ideas, proofs, and text of this document are completely human-generated.' and 'Chat GPT 5.6 Sol suggested the reference [4] for the reducedness of the standard equations defining the orbit closures, and was used to find spelling, grammatical, and minor mathematical errors.' The model is named exactly as the author wrote it.
events.delivers: Splitting and smoothness criteria for orbit closures of GL_n Arthur parameters; not a result on Arthur's conjectures as such.
events.remains: Not applicable to the bullet's conjectures.
events.time_since_posted: About 5 weeks; no human verification found.
events.direction: Neighbouring (GL_n Arthur parameters), no bearing on whether an Arthur conjecture is settled.

events.what_happened: Jeffrey Adams, Andrei Ionov, Lucas Mason-Brown, David Vogan, 'The Unitarity of Arthur Packets for Real Reductive Groups', arXiv:2606.01609, v1 submitted 1 Jun 2026, v2 revised 26 Sep 2026 (abstract opened; HTML opened to about 130,000 characters of about 169,000). Abstract (v1, as fetched): for a connected reductive G over R, Arthur conjectured packets of G(R); 'A longstanding conjecture, originally due to Arthur, is that all Arthur packets consist of unitary representations. In this paper, we prove this conjecture in general.' Main new tool: a Jordan decomposition realising each Arthur packet by real parabolic and cohomological induction from a unipotent Arthur packet on a Levi subgroup; unitarity then reduces to the unipotent case, cited as settled by Adams-Arancibia-Mezo, Adams-van Leeuwen-Miller-Vogan, Arthur, Barbasch, Barbasch-Ma-Sun-Zhu and Davis-Mason-Brown. Also: 'we also give a proof of Jiang's conjecture for real reductive groups' (upper bound on wavefront sets of members of an Arthur packet). The v2 comment (as fetched) says v2 generalises the main result to realise Arthur packets as induced representations and adds an appendix on Whittaker data and special positive systems. Acknowledgements (HTML, opened): thanks Chi-Heng Lo for suggesting the connection with Jiang's conjecture, and 'Jorg Schurmann for pointing out an error in an earlier version of this article'. The error is not described and I did not find it.
events.revisions: v2 26 Sep 2026: generalises the main result (Arthur packets as induced representations), adds appendix on Whittaker data and special positive systems, improves exposition (v2 comment, as fetched). An earlier version carried an error that a referee found (acknowledgements; not identified).
events.delivers: For connected reductive G over R: every Arthur packet G(R) consists of unitary representations (all packets, all real reductive groups, per the abstract's 'in general'). Also Jiang's conjecture for real reductive groups (upper bound on wavefront sets in terms of the Barbasch-Vogan dual of the Arthur SL2). Uses the unipotent case as an input from earlier work.
events.remains: Not claimed: non-archimedean unitarity of Arthur packets; the global multiplicity formula; the 1989 unipotent conjectures beyond the unitarity consequence. The bullet's local unitarity over non-archimedean fields is therefore not covered by this abstract.

checked_by.who: Pith automated AI review (reviewer identified on the page as grok-4.3)
checked_by.qualification: None: an automated T0 review; the page states no human expert has reviewed the paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Read the paper on 28 June 2026; verdict summarises the result as 'reducing via a new Jordan decomposition to the already-settled unipotent case'; Major 1 (section 3): the two-step induction must be shown to produce exactly the ABV packet, not a subset or superset; Major 2 (section 4): unitarity passing through the induction needs an explicit check that the packet axioms are preserved and no non-unitary constituents appear; six minor points. The page also contains a 'simulated' authors' rebuttal, which is not a real response.

events.time_since_posted: About 4 months (posted 1 Jun 2026, as of 11 Oct 2026). No human expert review found.
events.doubts: (1) Automated referee concerns on the two load-bearing steps (induction yields exactly the ABV packet; unitarity preserved by induction), as recorded above. (2) The acknowledgements say a referee found an error in an earlier version; the error is not described. (3) Scope changed between versions: v2 generalises the main result and adds appendices (per the v2 comment). (4) Adams gave a Fields talk on 11 Aug 2025 describing 'recent progress' on this unitarity question as in progress, and a Paris seminar abstract (seen in search, not opened) described the approach differently ('distinguished unipotent parameters'); the arXiv reduction is to Levi-subgroup unipotent packets. (5) The proof depends on the unipotent results of several authors, including Davis-Mason-Brown, whose paper I did not locate. (6) Yang's follow-up (yang-2026) reads the dependency of one lemma on AIMV's own appendix in one place and on an unpublished companion preprint in another; see that event.
events.direction: Confirms Arthur's conjectured unitarity for real reductive groups, in general, as stated in the abstract; the Jiang application is in the same direction. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Two talks at the Fields Institute on 11 Aug 2025, in the series 'Trace Formula, Endoscopic Classification and Beyond: the Mathematical Legacy of James Arthur' (opened: abstract pages). (a) Jeffrey Adams: a report on the Atlas project, including 'recent progress on proving Arthur's conjectures about the unitary of Arthur packets for real reductive groups', described as progress, not a completed proof. (b) David Vogan: proposes that for real reductive G, any unitary representation with integral infinitesimal character is an Arthur representation; the abstract reports, as of June 2025, that this holds for all representations of split G2, all but at most two of split F4, and all but at most six of split E7.
events.delivers: Talk-level progress on Arthur's unitarity conjecture for real groups (Adams, no details); Vogan's checks for split G2, F4 and E7 of a related but different conjecture (converse direction: unitary implies Arthur).
events.remains: All of the above, as far as these abstracts show; no written argument was found for either talk.
events.doubts: Talks, not written arguments; the Vogan checks are for finitely many groups of a different conjecture.
events.direction: Adams: in progress on the unitarity conjecture for real groups. Vogan: finite checks of a converse-direction conjecture, consistent with the picture.

events.what_happened: Devadatta G. Hegde, 'A simple construction of the automorphic residual spectrum', arXiv:2608.19129, v1 19 Aug 2026, single author (abstract page and HTML opened; HTML read in part). Main theorem (Section 1.2, as read): for a split semisimple group over a number field, the regularised spherical Borel Eisenstein series E*(rho kappa) is nonzero and square-integrable (the Kazhdan-Okounkov approach). Section 1.3 (as read) derives unitarity of the spherical constituent pi_{kappa,v} of an unramified principal series of a Chevalley group from this, and says this is Arthur's unitarity conjecture in that case. The abstract says 'a uniform and simple proof of Arthur's unitarity conjecture ... without case-by-case analysis or machine computation'. The intro credits the earlier cases to Miller (2013, computer-assisted), Halawi-Segal and Hundley-Miller. Talk at TIFR Number Theory Day, 20 Aug 2026 (search snippet, not opened).
events.delivers: Unitarity of the spherical (unramified) constituent of unramified principal series of split Chevalley groups over local fields, as Section 1.3 states it. The main theorem itself is global (residual spectrum).
events.remains: Non-spherical constituents; non-unramified packets; non-split groups; the wider unitarity conjecture. The abstract's wording ('proof of Arthur's unitarity conjecture') is broader than Section 1.3's unramified case.
events.time_since_posted: About 7 weeks; no human verification found.
events.doubts: Scope: the abstract and Section 1.3 describe different scopes (the case of unramified spherical constituents). The unramified case was already proved by Miller 2013 with computer help; the claimed novelty is the method. Single author, seven weeks old, unrefereed.
events.direction: Confirms the unramified/spherical case of Arthur's unitarity conjecture for split Chevalley groups; claimed as the general spherical case. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Jiawei Yang, 'The Arthur-Packet Support Equality for Real Reductive Groups', arXiv:2609.19197, v1 16 Sep 2026 (abstract page and HTML opened; HTML read to about the theorem statement). The microlocal packet of a real Arthur parameter psi is contained in the support of the two-step Jordan induction of the packet of its unipotent part psi_2, as shown by AIMV, who conjectured equality. Yang proves the reverse inclusion (abstract: 'We prove the reverse inclusion'). Method: positive translation, perverse devissage, singular support, coherent continuation.
events.delivers: The equality conjectured in AIMV (microlocal packet equals the support of the two-step Jordan induction) for real Arthur parameters, per the abstract.
events.remains: Nothing listed in the abstract for this equality. It is a structural statement about the microlocal packet, not one of Arthur's own conjectures.

checked_by.who: Pith automated AI review (reviewer identified on the page as deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash)
checked_by.qualification: None: an automated T0 review; the page states no human expert has reviewed the paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Written 18 Sep 2026. Verdict: the reverse inclusion closes the AIMV conjecture; well-structured; but Lemma 2.4 'relies on a theorem from an unpublished companion preprint' and Proposition 4.2 depends on it; recommends peer review. Minor points on typography.

events.time_since_posted: About 3.5 weeks; no human verification found.
events.doubts: Conflicting readings of the dependency: the Pith review says Lemma 2.4 rests on an unpublished companion preprint; the HTML body (as fetched, via a summariser) says Lemma 2.4's proof relies on '[AIMV26, Theorem A.2.1]', a specialisation of the three-parabolics theorem. If that citation is AIMV's own appendix, the dependency is on the June 2026 preprint (see adams-ionov-masonbrown-vogan-2026), not on a separate unpublished paper. The Pith review is an automated reading; I did not read the lemma itself.
events.direction: Proves the reverse inclusion of a support equality that AIMV conjectured; neither confirms nor refutes Arthur's conjectures directly.

events.what_happened: Sam Raskin, with Dennis Gaitsgory and Vincent Lafforgue: announced joint work on the Arthur-Ramanujan conjecture for unramified automorphic forms over function fields. Venue 1: Raskin's colloquium 'Geometric Langlands and the Arthur-Ramanujan conjecture', Princeton, 25 Feb 2026 (opened: abstract). Abstract: 'some recent progress, joint with Dennis Gaitsgory and Vincent Lafforgue ... provide a suitable version of the result for general reductive groups in the setting of unramified automorphic forms over function fields'; no explicit statement, no claim of completeness. Venue 2: a write-up for the ICM 2026 Proceedings, vol. 3 (SIAM), per search snippets; I could not open it (the PDF gave a certificate error). Per those snippets, the main result is the Arthur-Ramanujan conjecture on Hecke eigenvalue sizes and a categorified Arthur multiplicity formula in the l-adic setting, all forthcoming.
events.revisions: The full joint paper was not found; the ICM write-up's posting date is not established.
events.delivers: Announced: a version of the Arthur-Ramanujan bound for unramified automorphic forms over function fields, for general reductive groups (per the colloquium abstract). Not proved in any text I read.
events.remains: Everything beyond the announcement, and the number-field case, which is the one the bullet is about.
events.doubts: Forthcoming work, announced only. The setting is function fields in positive characteristic, not number fields. Arthur-Ramanujan is among the consequences the lead names, so this is a neighbouring question. The ICM text was not read.
events.direction: Announced in the direction of the Arthur-Ramanujan bound, for the function-field analogue; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Four manuscripts engage Arthur's conjectures. None proves a packet-level statement. (1) Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters: assuming the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition (its Theorem 1.1, cited as Parent), for each occurring excursion character nu of a split connected semisimple group over a global function field, at any full finite level, it constructs an algebraic SL_2 homomorphism phi_nu into the dual group, whose differential sends the raising element into the nilpotent orbit O_nu given by the decomposition, and a continuous homomorphism tau_nu from the Weil group W_U into the algebraic centralizer of phi_nu(SL_2), with reductive Zariski closure and eigenvalues of absolute value one at every complex embedding, such that after one fixed conjugation sigma_nu(w) = tau_nu(w) phi_nu(diag(a^deg(w), a^-deg(w))) for all w in W_U, inertia included. (2) Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level, unconditionally: for split semisimple G over a global function field, the cuspidal function space at any full finite level, with arbitrary divisor multiplicities, splits as a direct sum over nilpotent orbits of the dual group, both rationally and over Q-bar_ell. At level zero this proves Conjectures 3.4.5 and 3.4.6 of Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin. (3) Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration: for split connected semisimple G, under four characteristic conditions, the canonical filtration on finitely supported unramified automorphic functions is defined over Q for every closed invariant nilpotent support. The paper presents this as Conjecture 2.7.3 of Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin. Its cuspidal corollary identifies the level-zero cuspidal part with the rational orbit summands of (2), which the paper calls the common-scope form of Conjectures 3.4.9 and 3.4.11. (4) The Temperedness paper and Ramanujan-Arthur Corollary 1.2 give only generic-case temperedness, which the problem's lead names as a consequence of Arthur's conjectures; see the ramanujan-petersson-conjecture entry. The Restricted Geometric Langlands full-support manuscript and the three tame Hecke eigensheaf manuscripts do not bear on Arthur's conjectures. They concern geometric Langlands support and eigensheaves with tame unipotent monodromy, and make no claim about Arthur parameters, packets or SL_2 factors.
events.delivers: Each of (1)-(3) is a Galois-side or spectral-support structure over function fields for split groups: a commuting SL_2 and weight-zero centralizer pair recovering each occurring excursion parameter, an orbit decomposition of cusp spaces, and rationality of a canonical Arthur filtration. None states or proves the global Arthur packet decomposition of the discrete spectrum, local Arthur packets, unitarity of packet members, or the multiplicity formula. The Global Arthur paper says explicitly that it asserts no ellipticity, no Arthur-packet classification and no multiplicity formula. No manuscript claims to settle Arthur's conjectures. The family's result is function-field and split-group only, so the number-field content of the problem's lead is outside it. The text frames the commuting pair as the parameter-level part of V. Lafforgue's Arthur conjecture, whose elliptic form it does not prove. Whether the Galois-side pair counts as an Arthur-type parameter for the statement is for the judging pass to decide.
events.remains: If the claims are correct, the parts of the problem's list not covered are still open as far as this family goes: global and local Arthur packets and their character identities, Arthur's multiplicity formula, unitarity of packet members, the 1989 unipotent conjectures, and ellipticity of the global parameter (V. Lafforgue's version, not claimed here). For the generalized Ramanujan part, the family gives generic-case temperedness only. Also open: the enhancement is existential, with no uniqueness or multiplicity statement, and no link to packets is made.
events.doubts: (i) thm:parent in the Global Arthur paper is stated for occurring excursion characters, but the decomposition it cites (Theorem 1.1 of the Ramanujan-Arthur paper) is stated for joint eigencharacters of spherical Hecke operators at good places. The passage between the two is asserted with a citation; I did not verify it. (ii) The Global Arthur proof is a contradiction argument of about 5,400 lines. I did not read the lemmas it depends on, such as lem:tensor-nilpotence, prop:ind-qc-comparison and prop:open-orbit-enhancement. (iii) The Rationality paper flags a scope caveat itself: its pure Weil lift input (Theorem inp:pure-lift) is cited to a proposition stated for irreducible Weil parameters, and the paper uses a semisimple consequence recorded in a GLR appendix. A search of these manuscripts for sketch-type hedges found none in the parts that bear on Arthur's conjectures.; conditional on: Global Arthur Enhancements assumes the finite-level Ramanujan-Arthur decomposition (Theorem 1.1 of the Ramanujan-Arthur paper, restated there as thm:parent) and uses further results of that paper, cited as Parent: Sections 2-3, Lemma 6.4, Theorems 2.2-2.3, Propositions 2.5-2.7 and Lemma 3.6. It also cites external inputs: Xue's finiteness and smoothness theorems for stacks of shtukas, the nearby-cycle comparisons of Salmon and Eteve-Xue, Laurent Lafforgue's purity theorem, and Bezrukavnikov and Ben-Zvi-Chen-Helm-Nadler for the local coherent models. Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration assumes the four characteristic conditions of restricted geometric Langlands theory and uses the restricted equivalence and trace inputs of AGKRRV, Gaitsgory-Raskin and Raskin as cited. Its cuspidal corollary depends on the Ramanujan-Arthur paper (Theorem 1.1, Lemmas 6.1-6.2, Propositions 6.5-6.6, Remark 6.3).
events.direction: constructs Galois-side Arthur-type data over function fields (an SL_2 and weight-zero centralizer pair per occurring excursion parameter), proves an orbit decomposition of cusp spaces, and proves rationality of a canonical Arthur filtration; no packets
events.object: phi_nu: SL_2 into the dual group and tau_nu: W_U into the centralizer of phi_nu(SL_2), attached to each occurring excursion character. Constructed by an existence argument (the proof of Theorem thm:main proceeds by contradiction); not explicit.

summary: The bullet names only 'Arthur's conjectures' and links the Wikipedia stub of that name, so I read the statement through that lead as a family: a global multiplicity formula, local Arthur packets, unitarity (for real and non-archimedean groups), the 1989 unipotent conjectures, and their consequences. Since 26 Jan 2024 the main event is Adams, Ionov, Mason-Brown and Vogan (arXiv 2606.01609, 1 Jun 2026; revised 26 Sep 2026), which states that every Arthur packet of a connected reductive group over R consists of unitary representations ('In this paper, we prove this conjecture in general'), and also proves Jiang's conjecture for real groups. I read its abstract and about 130,000 of roughly 169,000 characters of HTML; the rest, including the reference list, was not readable through the fetcher. The acknowledgements thank Chi-Heng Lo and note a referee-found error in an earlier version (not identified). No human expert review, blog, or erratum was found; the only reviews are two automated AI-referee pages (Pith, grok-4.3, read 28 Jun 2026, with two major concerns about the induction step and the unitarity-passage step; and a deepseek-v4-flash review of the follow-up). The one later paper I found that builds on it (Yang, 16 Sep 2026) proves a support equality AIMV had conjectured, and the two sources I have disagree on whether that proof rests on AIMV's own appendix or on an unpublished companion preprint. Close call 1: the bullet's wording does not name unitarity, so whether AIMV settles 'Arthur's conjectures' turns on whether the local unitarity piece is part of the bullet, which the Wikipedia lead says it is, and on the non-archimedean side, which AIMV does not address. Close call 2: Hegde (arXiv 2608.19129, 19 Aug 2026) has a global main theorem and in Section 1.3 derives the unramified spherical case of unitarity; its abstract calls it a proof of Arthur's unitarity conjecture, which is broader than what Section 1.3 states. The global multiplicity formula for general reductive groups is not settled by any in-window event. In-window global and local work is for analogues (metaplectic: Li 2410.13606, Chen 2603.11602), for unitary or even orthogonal groups in generic or p-adic cases (Kim-Krishnamurthy-Shahidi 2506.00892; Hazeltine-Liu-Lo 2609.27261), or for single cases (Barchini-Lorincz 2512.07014 on F4(a3)). Dates before the window that matter: Arthur's 2013 book (classical groups), Miller 2012 (spherical unramified, exceptional groups, computer-assisted), Hundley-Miller 2019 (the Langlands element of unipotent packets, split real groups), Mason-Brown-Matvieievskyi 2021 with AMLV (unipotent unitarity, exceptional real groups; AMLV's own posting date not found), Chen-Zou 2021 (generic part, even orthogonal and unitary), Taibi 2015 (inner forms, regular character). AI: an AI search across the Arthur literature found one AI-disclosed paper (Balodis, 6 Sep 2026, on GL_n Arthur parameters, not an Arthur conjecture), in which the author states 'All the theorems, ideas, proofs, and text of this document are completely human-generated' and that 'Chat GPT 5.6 Sol' was used to suggest a reference and to check spelling and minor errors; that is not load-bearing and is recorded with systems empty. No event credits an AI system with mathematics. Computer work (Miller 2012 code, atlas computations, Adams's E7/E8 calculations) is computer-assisted, not AI. The DeepMind and OpenAI results from 2026 that the search turned up (Kakeya, Erdos unit distance) are unrelated and not recorded as events.
competing_reading: Against counting AIMV: the bullet names no unitarity conjecture, and the claim is one part of Arthur's program (real places, not p-adic, not global). It is an unrefereed four-month-old preprint, reviewed only by two automated AI referees, one of which flagged the two load-bearing steps (the induction yields exactly the ABV packet, and unitarity passes through induction). A referee also found an error in an earlier version, and v2 generalised the main result. The follow-up by Yang depends on AIMV's own appendix or on an unpublished preprint, depending on which of two sources is right. For counting: the Wikipedia lead explicitly lists unitary representations over local fields as part of the conjectures; AIMV claims the full real case 'in general' and reduces it to unipotent packets already settled by several groups; the authors are the Atlas group whose computations underlie most earlier unipotent cases; and Jiang's conjecture for real groups follows by the same method. Hegde: read as a proof of the full unitarity conjecture (abstract), it would be a second, independent route; read as Section 1.3 says, it covers only the unramified spherical constituents, which Miller 2013 had already covered with computer help.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A journal acceptance, or a written verification by a named expert, of AIMV's Jordan decomposition and of its induction-preserves-packets claim (the two steps the Pith review flagged). (2) The text of AIMV's Appendix A.2.1 and of Yang's Lemma 2.4, to settle whether Yang's dependency is on AIMV's appendix or on a separate unpublished preprint. (3) The AIMV reference list, to confirm Davis-Mason-Brown and AMLV, and the posting date of AMLV (the exceptional-group unitarity paper; the 2021 citation bounds it above). (4) Hegde's Section 1.3 read against the abstract: whether the claim is unramified-only. (5) A statement, from a survey or the authors, of what is known for p-adic Arthur packets and the global multiplicity formula for general reductive groups, since the bullet covers both. (6) The ICM 2026 write-up and the full Raskin-Gaitsgory-Lafforgue paper, to see whether the Arthur-Ramanujan result is proved and in which setting. (7) Full-text AI statements of the in-window neighbour papers, which I checked only at abstract or metadata level.

incomplete: (1) The AIMV paper (2606.01609): the fetcher read about 130,000 of about 169,000 characters of the HTML; the reference list and the end of the text were not read, so the AI and computer check there is partial. The PDF was unreadable. (2) Hegde (2608.19129) and Yang (2609.19197): only abstract pages and partial HTML were read; the acknowledgements and AI statements of these papers were not read in full. (3) AMLV: the exceptional-group paper was not located and its posting date is unknown; the record gives only an upper bound (2021). judgement.why: The statement names a family (global multiplicity formula, local packets, unitarity, unipotent conjectures), so no single event is whole. AIMV proves unitarity of all Arthur packets for real groups: a named part restricted to archimedean places, so case; it is unreviewed (Pith reviews are automated) but by established authors with no identified unanswered error, so credible. Hegde, Kim-Krishnamurthy-Shahidi (published), Barchini-Lorincz and Hazeltine-Liu-Lo 2026 settle restricted cases. Metaplectic work, Jiang and enhanced-Shahidi conjectures, and the function-field results (Raskin announcement, OpenAI family) concern changed questions: variant. The OpenAI family proves Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin conjectures and Galois-side structure over function fields, with no packets or multiplicity formula; it is generated by the README's own account, but variant. Reductions, definitional equivalences, conditional-hypothesis removals and talks are none.
judgement.doubts: Whether function-field results count as Arthur's conjectures (the lead speaks of adele rings generally) was a close call; I read the OpenAI family as variant because what it proves is GLR's conjectures and Galois-side data, not packets or multiplicity. AIMV's earlier-version error and the v2 scope change are noted but not treated as an unanswered error. Taibi's journal publication is from a snippet only, left unreviewed.
